_comment: What mux-activity reads: every pane of the multiplexer it runs in - Rex, Herdr or Luvus - through that multiplexer's CLI, read-only. A rex_panes, herdr_panes or luvus_panes section from before is read when there is no mux_activity section.
_backend_comment: Which multiplexer to read. auto finds out from the pane mux-activity runs in: REX_SESSION and REX_BLOCK for Rex, HERDR_ENV=1 for Herdr, LUVUS_ENV=1 for Luvus, and the nearest of them in the process tree when several are set. The --mux flag overrides this.
_rex_server_comment: Which Rex server to read: a host label from `rex hosts`, or an address. Empty means the CLI's own default - REX_SERVER when it is set, else this machine's server. Set, it is read from anywhere, inside a multiplexer or not. CPU and memory are shown only for this machine's server.
_luvus_session_comment: Under Luvus, which Luvus server session to read. `luvus session list` names the ones on this machine; `default` is the one `luvus` starts on its own.
_refresh_comment: Maximum idle delay in seconds; Rex events wake a full read sooner.
_agents_comment: Command names that count as coding agents under Rex, Herdr and Luvus. Under Herdr and Luvus, any agent the multiplexer itself reports always shows; this list fills gaps for panes the multiplexer did not recognise. Matched against the pane's foreground program or process tree, and under Rex against the app name a program reports with OSC 7501 (aliases such as claude-code and antigravity-cli resolve through the shared catalogue). Generic names (forge, agent, cn, vibe) match by default only with an install or script path clue; add a name here to match it unconditionally.
